scoring_justification: Checker compares agent-reported band gaps and Seebeck coefficients to paper values (within tolerances). Power factor verified by structural trend (max p-type PF of any PSTS lower than CoSb₃).

hidden_assets.purpose: Gold band gaps and Seebeck coefficient values for comparison
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper: Physical Review B 85, 245211 (2012). Band gaps: ranges 0.41-0.61 eV (PSTS), 0.22 eV (CoSb₃) from Sec IV and Fig.2. Seebeck: 258 µV/K for p-type CoGe₁.₅S₁.₅ at 10²⁰ cm⁻³, -307 µV/K for n-type CoSn₁.₅Te₁.₅ at 10²⁰ cm⁻³, from Sec IV.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Values taken from paper text and produce the exact numbers the reference solve.sh writes.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: Every value directly traceable to the paper's reported quantities for the specified compounds and conditions.

outputs.description: Direct band gap values for the six PSTS compounds and CoSb₃, compared against paper‑reported reference values within an allowed tolerance.
Seebeck coefficient at 300 K for p‑type CoGe₁.₅S₁.₅ at a hole concentration of 10²⁰ cm⁻³, compared against the paper's implied reference value.
Seebeck coefficient at 300 K for n‑type CoSn₁.₅Te₁.₅ at an electron concentration of 10²⁰ cm⁻³, compared against the paper's implied reference value.
Power factor as a function of chemical potential at 300 K. Verified by a structural audit: the maximum p‑type power factor of any PSTS must be lower than that of CoSb₃.

output_contract.notes: All outputs are produced from the same DFT+DFPT+Wannier+Boltzmann workflow, ensuring internal consistency. Phonon and Born effective charge calculations are included as process steps.
